design.title: Continuous vantages: every training framing is shifted by a fresh random offset of up to ±12 px, so over an epoch the training views cover the ground continuously instead of standing on the fixed 24 m lattice
design.eli5: Until now the model studied Berlin from a fixed grid of spots 24 metres apart, the same spots every time, so it could partly memorise 'how this exact framing of this exact photo looks'. Now every time it studies a place, the camera is nudged a random few metres sideways first, so it never sees exactly the same picture twice. It has to learn what the place looks like, not what one framing looks like, and that should carry better to a photograph it has never seen.
design.hypothesis: Champion exp 20 (0.0777): on held-out truedop_2024, usable 93.0%, false fix 0.75%, abstain 6.25%. The same eval viewpoints on the three training photographs score 100% usable / 0% false. Every position-sampling choice in this era has been the same: train.py shows each place only at the 72,712 exact lattice centres, 24 px apart, with heading as the only geometric variation. So each lattice framing appears three times per epoch (once per survey) at the same pixel-exact framing, over 8 epochs. A network with ~31 MB of weights can fit that discrete set of framings as framing-plus-survey fingerprints. That fit costs nothing on the training photographs (100%) but gives no structural invariance on a new photograph. Every eval view stands 11-17 m off-lattice, so on 2024 the model faces a new photograph AND an unseen framing at once. Its remaining abstentions are where the two members' beliefs stop agreeing. CLAUDE.md's Prignitz-detour record names this exact mechanism, continuous-vantage training with ±12 px jitter, as 'designed and implemented; never trained' and as the natural next move. That detour also showed that whatever fixes look-alike confusions has to act during training, not at decode time. This era has never touched how training positions are sampled; arch_json shows every change in exps 12-21 went to the trunk, head, augmentation pixels or weight schedule. Hypothesis: re-drawing each framing at a continuous random offset every time it is used makes any two uses of a place differ in framing. That removes the pixel-exact framing fingerprint as a solution and pushes both members toward the layout that survives a shift, which is also what survives a change of survey. The result should be more members agreeing on 2024, and so fewer abstentions. Note, stated plainly: with ±12 px jitter some training framings on the TRAINING photographs fall close to eval vantages. That is legitimate (deployment views are arbitrary vantages over mapped ground, and §4 says the model is shown all of its box), but it makes the logged train_capture_diagnostics less informative as a viewpoint test. The scored question, a never-seen photograph, is untouched: truedop_2024 is never loaded. Experiment 21 (LP-FT) is not re-run here. It died on a laptop DNS failure during its final epoch, so its verdict is void, but its training curves through epoch 7 matched exp 20's to the third decimal (top1 0.9062 vs 0.9056, xs_cos_same 0.783 vs 0.787), so a re-run is expected to land within noise.
